# Relimie

> Relimie is a mindful drinking and alcohol tracking app. It works as an alcohol diary and drinking-habit tracker, helping moderate and sober-curious drinkers track alcohol consumption against a personal baseline, understand emotional triggers through a diary, analyze habits, estimate blood alcohol (promille) after a night out, and break cravings with a guided 4-7-8 breathing exercise — without guilt or judgment. It is a natural companion for cutting down on drinking, Dry January, and Sober October.

The core method is "baseline-drinking": a personal long-term average rather than a rigid daily limit. The Orb on the Home Screen shows at a glance whether the user is within their baseline (Green), slightly over (Gold), or needs to pause (Red).

- [User Guide](https://relimie.com/en/guide.html): Complete feature documentation covering the Orb, drink logging, diary, analytics, and data export.
- [FAQ](https://relimie.com/en/faq.html): Common questions about baseline tracking, logging, the Cravings Breaker, and data privacy.
- [Cravings Breaker](https://relimie.com/en/cravings.html): How the 4-7-8 breathing circuit breaker works for craving disruption.
- [Promille / Blood Alcohol Calculator](https://relimie.com/en/promille-calculator.html): Interactive blood alcohol calculator and a full explanation of the Widmark formula, including how long alcohol takes to clear and how accurate such an estimate really is.
- [What's New](https://relimie.com/en/whats_new.html): Release notes, newest first. Relimie is now available on Android via Google Play (the full app, feature-identical to iOS). Latest release v2.2.0 — blood alcohol estimate with time to clear, per-drink icons under the Orb, rebuilt consumption overview, guided tours on every page.
- [Privacy Policy](https://relimie.com/en/privacy.html): Full data privacy documentation. All data is stored locally on device only.
- [Support](https://relimie.com/en/support.html): Contact information for support.

## Articles

Judgement-free, informational guides on mindful drinking. Each targets a common question and is a top-of-funnel entry point (also available in German at /de/ and Russian at /ru/).

- [Sober After Vacation: How Many Sober Days Bring You Back?](https://relimie.com/en/sober-after-vacation.html): What a week of all-inclusive drinking adds up to in grams of pure alcohol, and how to turn it into a finish line. Works the sum through: ~110 g/day across seven nights is ~770 g against a 20 g/day baseline, leaving ~630 g above the line and about 32 sober days to bring the average back. Covers backfilling a trip roughly rather than perfectly, three ways to run it as a challenge (your exact number, a round thirty days, or a calendar month such as October), and states plainly that the days-to-baseline figure is arithmetic on the user's own logged inputs, not a health timeline.
- [Promille Calculator: Blood Alcohol and How Long Until You're Sober](https://relimie.com/en/promille-calculator.html): An interactive blood alcohol calculator plus a full explanation of the Widmark formula (c = A / (m x r), r = 0.7 male / 0.6 female / 0.65 unspecified, elimination 0.15 permille per hour). Covers converting drinks to grams of pure alcohol, why nothing speeds up sobering up, and an honest account of accuracy: the estimate deliberately errs toward a higher value and a longer wait (no absorption correction, whole day counted at once, durations rounded up, body weight never guessed). Explicitly not a fitness-to-drive test.
- [Am I Drinking Too Much?](https://relimie.com/en/am-i-drinking-too-much.html): How to tell where you stand by comparing your own long-term average (built over ~3 months of tracking) against average daily alcohol intake by country and national low-risk guidelines. Explains why a single day cannot be compared to an average.
- [How Many Calories Are in Alcohol?](https://relimie.com/en/calories-in-alcohol.html): Calories in wine, beer and spirits compared, why alcohol calories add up, and how to track them without giving up the glass you enjoy.
- [All articles](https://relimie.com/en/articles.html): The full mindful-drinking article hub.

## App Details

- Platform: iOS (Apple App Store, App ID: 6759795714) and Android (Google Play, package com.ikaengel.relimie)
- Download (iOS): https://apps.apple.com/us/app/relimie-track-alcohol-limits/id6759795714
- Download (Android): https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.ikaengel.relimie
- YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@RelimieApp
- Languages: English, German, Russian
- Current version: 2.2.0
- Privacy model: Zero cloud storage, no third-party analytics, no cookies, no account required
- Pricing: Free core features (logging, analytics); optional premium subscription for advanced analytics

## Core Features

- **Personal Baseline**: A long-term drinking average (not a rigid daily limit) that acts as an anchor for habit change. Data from WHO recommendations and country/gender averages help users choose their starting baseline.
- **Emotional Trigger Diary**: Log how you feel before drinking, the morning after, and on sober days. Contextual tags surface automatically — Triggers (stress, boredom, social pressure), After-Effects (hangover, anxiety, clarity), Sober Feelings (productivity, pride, energy).
- **Drink Logging**: Track pure alcohol, calories, and spending per drink. AI Sparkle button auto-fills ABV and calories for unknown drinks. Prices preset by country average.
- **Analytics Hub**: History, overview, habits graph, trends by day/time, and a chronological heatmap. Rotate the phone to landscape for a full-screen consumption chart over time. Export as PDF ("Share My Story") or JSON backup. All data stays on device.
- **Blood Alcohol Estimate**: On any day with logged drinks, a button next to the Orb opens a rough per mille estimate calculated from what was logged, plus how long it takes to clear. Uses the Widmark formula with body weight and gender. Free for every user, not part of Premium. It is an estimate, never a measurement, and never a basis for deciding to drive.
- **Cravings Breaker**: Long-press the Orb to trigger a guided 4-7-8 breathing exercise (inhale 4s, hold 7s, exhale 8s) with inspirational quotes. Acts as a mental circuit breaker. The same screen shows a free Body Recovery Timeline counting what the body regains since the last drink.
